newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Rains, lower money rates boost Zimbabwe stocks.
newsitem.headline: Rains, lower money rates boost Zimbabwe stocks.

text.p: A continuing shift of cash from the money to the equity market and weekend rains boosted Zimbabwean stocks on Monday with brokers saying they recorded an "explosion" of volumes across the board.
"What we saw was an explosion of volumes across the board. We saw as much as Z$30 to Z$40 million traded today and that's usually lucky if we see that in a week," one broker said.
"The market was encouraged by the rains and the continuing shift of liquidity from the money market into the equity market," another one said.
The key industrial index rose 35.70 points to close at 7,969.73.

Among the day's winners, pharmaceutical group Caps gained 50 cents to 350, farm implements-maker Zimplow climbed 40 cents to 400 as did horticulture firm Ariston to 1,490 while timber producer Border and finance group Finhold each added 25 cents to 1,275 and 975 respectively.

Publishing group Zimpapers at 2,000, clothing and furniture retailer Tedco at 650 and sugar producer Hippo at 870 all gained 20 cents while 10-cent additions were recorded in a string of other counters, notably hotel chain Zimsun to 410.

Minings traded lighter with gold producer Ashanti surging 500 cents to 13,500 while Wankie Colliery added five cents to 380. Falgold eased five cents to 135, leaving the mining index 2.84 points lower at 1,215.91.
